summary: Record one semantic command per committed user intention and restore every coupled state field together on undo or redo.
objective: A continuous preview becomes one undoable command, cancellation creates none, and undo restores model state rather than only its current rendering.
applies_when: An interactive editor or configurator offers undo and a single action can change transforms, hierarchy, occupancy, annotations or derived views together.
intent_signals: one drag creates hundreds of undo steps
undo restores mesh but not occupied socket
example_prompts: Make moving and reparenting a module one undoable editor action.
Undo an annotation move together with its anchor and label metadata.
negative_signals: reuse browser text history as scene history
not_for: Immutable playback with no editing history.
Distributed collaborative undo, which requires an explicit concurrency model beyond this profile.

principles: History records semantic model operations, not raw input events or animation frames. Begin and preview are provisional; commit is the history boundary.
A command owns all coupled state it changes: model values, parentage, local transforms, occupancy, selected IDs and annotation anchors where applicable.
Use a validated inverse when the operation is truly invertible; otherwise retain sufficient before state. Both paths restore authoritative state and regenerate views.
Undo and reset are separate: undo walks committed history, redo reapplies an undone command, and reset returns to a declared baseline under its own policy.
implementation: At interaction begin, create a transaction with target IDs and the minimum complete before state. Update a derived preview without appending history entries.
On commit, revalidate, capture after state, apply coupled writes atomically and append one command. On cancel or failure, restore before state and discard the transaction.

Undo through the same model mutation boundary, then derive hierarchy, transforms, selection and visuals. Redo reuses the stored command; a new divergent commit clears the redo branch unless the product explicitly exposes branching history.
Keep scene history separate from focused text-field history. Input adapters decide whether an undo signal belongs to text editing, the scene or neither.
Label destructive or non-reversible external effects separately; this local scene-history profile must not imply it can reverse network publication or file overwrite.
observable_checks: Drag through many preview updates and commit once; history grows by one, then undo and redo restore exact before and after model states.
Cancel, lose capture before commit and fail validation in separate trials; none changes history or leaves coupled state partially updated.
Move and reparent a nested object with an occupied socket, then undo; parent, local transform, world result and both occupancy maps return together.
Undo, make a different commit and invoke redo; behavior follows the declared branch policy without resurrecting an invalid command.

creative_affordances: Show concise action labels or a scrub-able local history when it helps users understand reversibility.
Animate undo from restored model states without making animation frames authoritative.
known_limits: Input Events historyUndo and historyRedo concern editing hosts and do not implement custom 3D history.
Memory bounds, persistence and collaborative conflict resolution are product-specific.
Authored and source-checked guidance; no undo runtime was executed.

claims.statement: Input Events Level 2 defines historyUndo as an intention to undo the last editing action and historyRedo as an intention to redo the last undone editing action for editing hosts.
claims.scope: W3C Working Draft text-input event vocabulary only; it does not specify transaction boundaries or a custom 3D scene history implementation.
